chapter.title: USB
chapter.sub: A camera leaves calls “randomly”. The user thinks IT is laughing at her. IT thinks she's unplugging it. Both are wrong.
chapter.status: **DRAFT** · scripted from the season map ahead of its production-bible entry · IDs provisional

items.text: SEASON 3 · EPISODE 3 · DRAFT  Parallel lenses · Rhea, Sam and Priya · Level L3  A camera leaves calls “randomly”. The user thinks IT is laughing at her. IT thinks she keeps unplugging it. Three views of the same Wednesday.  ⚑ RV-62: USB behavior is simplified. RV-65: a user who feels blamed. Some choices run on a clock.

items.title: She Keeps Unplugging It
items.stakes: Rhea's camera leaves calls “randomly.” IT decided she's the problem. She's three weeks into a new job, and she's starting to believe them.
items.reward: An apology Rhea deserves, and fourteen more rooms that stop dropping.

objectives.text: Look closer: two things Rhea wrote down

items.rumor: Forty-one camera tickets, all closed “user error.” Nobody ever asked a user for their notes.

items.alt: The Studio Room: a design review slide fills the display. A red label under it reads CAMERA: NOT FOUND. Rhea, at the head of the table, throws up her hands. A yellow sticker on the table edge says CAMERA GONE? REPLUG HERE.

bubbles.text: Rhea, we lost you again. Just the slides now.

items.caption: Rhea Castillo, three weeks into running design research. Twelve people remote. Fourth time this month.

items.alt: Rhea reaches to the table cubby under the sticker, unplugs the cable and plugs it back in. The camera label is gone; the camera is back.

bubbles.text: Unplug. Count to five. Plug in. Like the sticker says.

items.caption: It comes back. It always comes back. Nobody has ever told her why.

items.alt: At her desk, Rhea reads ticket #3, resolved: cause, user unplugged camera; please do not unplug room devices. Below it, a support chat message shared by mistake: studio room again, she's unplugging it, lol.

bubbles.text: They think I'm pulling cables out of the table. I'm the one plugging them back IN.

items.caption: New job, new team, and IT has decided she's the problem.

lines.text: They think I'm pulling cables out of the table. I'm the one plugging them back IN.
I've started wondering if I'm bad at this job.

items.prompt: Rhea's 3 p.m. review. Ten minutes in, the camera vanishes again. Twelve people are waiting. What should she do?
items.happening: The camera vanished ten minutes into her presentation.
known: ◉ Replugging the table hub brings it back
items.risk: Twelve people's hour, and Rhea's standing with her new team.
timeout: Rhea freezes. The team waits, then someone says “let's reschedule.”
A known workaround plus a written time was the whole answer.

hints.text: The workaround works. What would make the next person believe you?

options.label: Replug at the sticker — and write down the exact time
options.result: Five seconds, the camera's back, and a line in her notebook: “Wed 15:11, presenting ~10 min, video paused.”
options.consequence: The meeting goes on, and someone now has evidence.

options.label: Restart the room computer
options.result: Four minutes of a black screen. Twelve people drift off to email.
options.consequence: It comes back — and the computer's record of the drop is gone.
options.fail: A restart costs the meeting and erases the one log that could clear her.

options.label: Carry on without the camera
options.result: Slides only. The team can't see her face when she asks the hard question.
options.consequence: It works; it costs something real.

options.label: Pull and replug every cable in the cubby
options.result: Content share drops, the laptop input drops, the speaker bar re-enumerates. Two minutes of chaos.
options.consequence: Several changes at once: nobody can say which one mattered.
options.fail: Changing everything at once proves nothing and breaks what was working.

items.text: ✦ UX RULE #24 · AVERY'S LENS  User error is design error  When people keep 'doing it wrong', the design is teaching them wrong.  The camera 'vanished' because of a sleep setting, not because Rhea unplugged things.

items.alt: Rhea's notebook: camera gone Monday 9:40, Wednesday 10:14 and 15:11 — all design reviews, about ten minutes in; all while she was presenting with video paused. Is it me?
items.caption: She starts keeping times. Nobody asked her to.

items.title: Timestamps, to the second
items.body: *10:14:03 camera gone. 10:16:40 replugged. 10:18 back.* Seven meetings, all the same shape. She wasn't collecting evidence. She was collecting proof she wasn't crazy.

items.alt: Sam at his desk points at the room computer's USB event log: 10:14:03 camera removed; 10:16:40 table hub removed; 10:16:41 table hub added; 10:16:48 camera added, new instance.

bubbles.text: Device removed. Device removed. Every time. She's yanking the cable. Case closed.

items.caption: Sam reads the log the way he reads everything: fast.

lines.text: Device removed. Device removed. Every time. Case closed.
…I don't do slowly. It's a whole personality.

items.sub: Beginner · the skill behind this chapter

items.alt: A teaching moment: Ines and Maya beside a board. Focus is making the subject sharp. Autofocus loves big flat walls; it doesn't love people. So where should it focus? On the people: wall distance minus the gap. Wall at six metres, people one and a half in front: four and a half metres.

bubbles.text: Focus is making the subject sharp. Autofocus loves big flat walls; it doesn't love people.
So where should it focus?
On the people: wall distance minus the gap. Wall at six metres, people one and a half in front: four and a half metres.

items.caption: Beginner: the term, what it means, the formula — and one worked example out loud.

items.text: 📘 RAY'S NOTEBOOK · BEGINNER  Terms    Focus   Adjusting the lens so the subject is sharp.   Resolution   How many pixels a picture has across and down.   Formula, variables and a worked example   ƒ FORMULA · Distance to the subject  d subject  = d wall  − d gap    d wall   camera to the wall behind  d gap   how far the subject stands in front of that wall    Worked example.  Wall 6 m from the camera, presenter 1.5 m in front of it: focus at 4.5 m.
📒 EMPATHIA LEARN FIELDBOOK · MODULE 24 OF 31 · P. 32  PART 1 CORE TECHNOLOGY FOUNDATIONS · PART 2 AV NETWORKING & DATA  Page 32. Maya: “A meeting room is a tiny venue nobody staffs.”

items.label: **Fix-It Lab:** the room camera wakes up wrong. Set it right.

items.alt: Sam rubs his eyes. A label reads: Sam's queue, 41 open. Maya pulls up a chair.

bubbles.text: Forty-one tickets. I don't have time to watch someone unplug a camera.
Then give me two minutes. Read me the times again. Slowly.

items.prompt: Ticket #4 from the Studio Room. Sam wants to close it. What do you do?
items.happening: Four tickets. A log full of “removed”.

options.label: Close it as user error with a firmer note
options.result: Rhea gets: “Resolved. Please stop unplugging room equipment.”
options.consequence: She stops reporting. The camera keeps leaving.
options.fail: Closing the ticket doesn't close the fault. It closes the channel that would have told you about it.

options.label: Swap the camera
options.result: A new camera, same disappearance ten idle minutes later.
options.consequence: An hour and a camera spent on the wrong suspect.
options.fail: Swapping parts before reading the evidence is fix-by-guess.

options.label: Line up the log's timestamps with Rhea's notebook
options.result: Camera removed 10:14:03. Rhea's replug 10:16:40. Her notebook: presenting, video paused, about ten minutes in.
options.consequence: The order of events clears her — and points at what the room was doing.

options.label: Zip-tie the table cable so she can't unplug it
options.result: Rhea can no longer bring her camera back.
options.fail: You treated the person fixing it as the cause.

items.alt: System View timeline from the room log: 10:04 presenting with video paused; 10:14:03 camera removed while nobody touched anything; 10:16:40 table hub replugged by Rhea following the sticker; 10:16:48 camera added as a new device.
items.caption: The camera left first. The replug came two and a half minutes later.

items.alt: Maya taps the first line. Sam's face falls.

bubbles.text: The camera left at 10:14:03. The hub moved at 10:16:40. She didn't unplug it, Sam. She's the one plugging it back.
…Oh no.

items.title: She isn't causing it. She's fixing it.
items.body: Every “removed” in the log that Sam read as Rhea yanking a cable comes minutes AFTER the camera had already gone. Her replug is the recovery, not the fault — and the sticker that taught her to do it is Sam's own workaround from last year.
items.label: Test: what does the timeline rule out, and what do you do next?

items.alt: Sam and Maya in the empty Studio Room, looking at the yellow sticker on the table edge.

bubbles.text: I wrote that sticker. Last year. Then I closed her tickets for doing what it says.
Then you know exactly who to talk to first.

items.prompt: I wrote that sticker. Then I closed her tickets for doing what it says. What do I even say to her?

options.label: “Say it plainly: it wasn't you, we got it wrong, here's what we're doing.”
options.reply: Plainly. Okay. I can do plainly.

options.label: “Maybe let me handle it.”
options.reply: …No. It's my ticket. I'll do it.

options.label: “Just reopen the ticket. She'll see.”
options.reply: She won't see. Nobody reads ticket updates. That's the whole problem.

items.alt: Sam at Rhea's desk. She looks up, guarded.

bubbles.text: I closed your tickets as user error. It wasn't you. I'm sorry — and the chat message was worse.
I thought I was the new manager who can't work a camera. Thank you for saying it out loud.

lines.text: I thought I was the new manager who can't work a camera.
You're the manager who kept better logs than IT.

items.text: 🔭 PHYSICS IN MOTION  The camera that looks at the back wall  The science under this episode’s problem — live.

items.alt: Maya kneels by Rhea's desk; Rhea holds out her notebook.

bubbles.text: Your times are better than our logs. They say what the room was doing. Can I borrow them?
Nobody's ever asked for them.

items.alt: At the operations wall, Priya shows the switch port feeding the Studio Room's USB extender: link up since Monday 6 a.m., zero drops, power steady.

bubbles.text: The extender's port never blinked. Link steady, power steady. Whatever leaves, it isn't my network.
Then it's inside the room — between the camera and the computer.

items.title: Kepler explains the eye
items.body: In 1604 Johannes Kepler showed that the eye's lens forms an upside-down image on the retina — the eye is a camera. Small meeting-room cameras use tiny focal lengths so that almost everything is in focus; the math is Kepler's.

items.alt: Priya lays out three sources as labels — Rhea's notebook, the room computer log, the switch port — adding up to: ten idle minutes.

bubbles.text: Three clocks. Her notebook, the room log, my switch. Every drop: ten minutes after her camera goes idle.
Idle for ten minutes. Something is putting it to sleep.

items.title: Link steady · power steady
items.body: Her port never blinked. Priya adds one line to the shared notes: *not the network — inside the room — something is putting it to sleep.* Under it, Sam writes: *a Sunday update?* Nobody answers him.

items.prompt: 4:35. You're reproducing it: slides up, video paused. Minute ten — the camera just vanished. What now, before anyone touches anything?
items.happening: Reproduced: camera gone after ten idle minutes.
timeout: Sam, trying to help, replugs the table hub. The camera comes back and the moment is gone.
A reproduction is only worth something if you read it while it's failing.

hints.text: You made it fail on purpose. Read the failure before it goes away.

options.label: Priya bounces the extender's switch port
options.result: The extender re-powers and the camera comes back. The computer's view of the failure is gone.
options.consequence: It's her network, so she may — but the live state you waited ten minutes for is lost.
options.fail: You spent ten minutes making it fail, then erased the failure.

options.label: Read the room computer's device list and power settings right now
options.result: Camera: not present. Extender: present. Power plan: energy saving — suspend idle USB devices after 10 minutes. Set by room image v4, last month.
options.consequence: Caught in the act: the computer suspended an idle camera that didn't wake cleanly through the extender.

options.label: Replug the table hub
options.fail: The workaround is for meetings. This was your test.

options.label: Swap the extender
options.result: Twenty minutes with a spare. It may help; nobody will know why.
options.consequence: Fix-by-guess on the most expensive part.

items.alt: The room computer's power and device screen: power plan energy saving; USB suspend when idle; idle timeout 10 minutes; set by room image v4 last month; camera not present; extender present.
items.caption: A laptop setting, on a computer that is a room.

evidence.label: suspend idle USB after 10 min · image v4

items.alt: System View: the camera at the display connects through a powered extender and 25 metres of cable to the room computer. The computer's power plan suspends idle USB after ten minutes; the wake-up doesn't pass cleanly through the extender; the camera re-enumerates as a new instance; the conferencing software still looks for the old one and reports no camera. Replugging the table hub re-enumerates everything and the camera is found again.
items.caption: Symptom: Signal (no video). Causes: Power (device power state) + Configuration.

items.label: **Learn it now:** USB, cameras and room computers — enumeration, power budgets, sleep and extenders.

items.alt: Sam at his laptop, editing the managed room profile. Maya beside him.

bubbles.text: Profile v4.1: no USB suspend on room computers. Software picks “the room camera”, not that one exact camera.
Now we try to break it the way it breaks. Ten idle minutes, twice.

items.alt: In the Studio Room, Rhea turns her video back on after fifteen idle minutes. The camera answers at once. A label reads: idle 15:00, video on, check.

bubbles.text: Rhea, we can see you. Both times.

items.caption: Proof under the exact condition that failed, confirmed from the far end.

items.alt: Priya shows a ticket search: camera tickets in rooms with the same extender — fourteen rooms plus the Studio Room, 37 tickets, every one resolved as user error. Sam closes his eyes.

bubbles.text: Same extender in fourteen more rooms. Thirty-seven camera tickets. Every one closed “user error”.
…Most of them by me.

items.title: It was never one room. It was fifteen, closed one at a time.
items.body: The “random” camera in the Studio Room is a fleet-wide pattern: every room with the long extender and the new image does the same thing. Nobody saw it because each ticket was closed as one user's mistake — thirty-seven times.
items.label: Test: you have Sam's eight hours this week. Fund the plan that retires the most risk.

items.prompt: Studio Room proven. Fourteen more rooms share the extender. How do you roll out profile v4.1?
items.happening: The fix works in one room; the pattern is in fifteen.

options.label: Push it to all three hundred rooms tonight
options.result: Every room computer takes the change at once. Two rooms with a different camera stop showing video at all.
options.consequence: Nobody can say which rooms broke because of it until Monday.
options.fail: Never test on everyone at once.

options.label: Ring by ring: Studio + two extender rooms + one room without, idle test each; then the fourteen; then the fleet
options.result: Four rooms Thursday, fourteen Friday, the rest next week — each with the ten-minute idle test.
options.consequence: Small, known, provable steps — including one room that should NOT change.

options.label: Only the Studio Room — the others haven't complained lately
options.result: They haven't complained because they were told it was them.

options.label: Replace every extender first
options.result: Three weeks for parts, a big invoice, and the power plan still suspends idle USB.
options.consequence: The trigger is in the profile, not the box.

items.label: **Service Mode:** run the Studio Room yourself before Rhea's 3 p.m. review.

items.text: 📁 CASE FILE · CASE-021 · SIGNAL original  The Camera That Leaves  Thirty-seven tickets closed as “user error.” The user was the one fixing it.   Open the case file ▸   Learn · Service · Engineer — it doesn't change your story progress.

items.alt: Change log entry 3: Studio camera left after ten idle minutes because of image v4's USB suspend; profile v4.1 disables suspend and selects the camera by type, idle test twice with the far end confirming; fourteen rooms share the extender with 37 tickets closed as user error, now reopened; Rhea told; sticker replaced; thanks to Rhea's notebook and Priya's port log.
The Studio Room table: the old sticker is replaced by a blue label — camera left? Note the time, call x4400. Rhea holds up the old yellow sticker; Sam grins.

bubbles.text: Can I keep the old sticker?
Frame it. Label it “Sam's worst idea”.

items.caption: A workaround that asks for evidence instead of hiding it.

items.alt: Late. Sam alone at his desk, eyes closed, in front of a screen: closed this month, 612 — fastest on the team.

bubbles.text: Six hundred and twelve closed. How many of them were actually closed?

items.caption: He doesn't say it to anyone. Not yet.

lines.text: Six hundred and twelve closed. How many were actually closed?
(He doesn't say it to anyone. He says it to the queue, which doesn't answer.)

items.label: **Class match:** one symptom — “the camera's gone” — many causes. Where did each one live?

items.alt: Ines, the CEO's executive assistant, run sheet on a clipboard, stops at Maya's desk.

bubbles.text: The CEO's town hall is Thursday. Nineteen minutes of it will be remote-only. Don't make me nervous.

items.caption: Next: *Town Hall.*

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  “Random” usually means “we haven't lined up the clocks yet.” Read logs slowly: a line says what the computer saw, not who did it. Line the log up with the user's own record and with an independent clock, reproduce the failure under its real condition and read it while it's failing, fix it in the managed profile, and prove it under the same condition from the far end. Then ask how many other rooms were closed as “user error”.

REFLECTION (optional)  · Rhea and Sam were both wrong about each other, and both were doing their best with what they could see. Whose side of a problem have you only ever seen from your own lens?  Boundary: this reflection doesn't prove anything about the camera.
